depth.transferChallenge: Change one value, type, or boundary in the sample. Write the exact stdout or diagnostic you expect before asking rustc. Keep the focus on string, &str, chars, and bytes.

writing.exampleCaption: Bytes and characters are different counts, and Rust makes you pick.
writing.explanation: String owns a growable UTF-8 buffer and &str borrows one. Because a character can be several bytes, s[0] is not allowed at all: you choose .bytes(), .chars(), or a byte range you know lands on a boundary. That refusal is the point — it makes an entire class of encoding bug impossible.
writing.feedback: len() reports UTF-8 bytes, which is larger than the character count here.
writing.question: Which gives the number of characters?
writing.rule: len() is bytes; use .chars() when you mean characters.
